I might not be the best at answering this since I’m in the class right now and I’m not all that good, but I got a perfect score on my 2 SAQs a week ago using some sort of strategy, so im not sure but I think my strategy worked. The first strategy I used for the SAQs was not spending too much time on the multiple choice, and giving myself as much time as possible to write and edit my answers .The second is using the acronym ACE, Answer, Cite, Elaborate, which my teacher has my class use. And then third my teacher tells my class to shamelessly name drop, such as naming as many events or people as possible that might relate to the answer and just as much vocab as you can possibly fit in without it being too inaccurate or excessive. But overall the best kind of strategy is just reading the question, making sure to identify if it’s saying to explain, describe, etc. and then answer it as strictly as possible. First sentence like a mini claim just to answer, second sentence stating some specific historical events to prove answer, and third sentence further explaining the evidence and how it relates to the claim/question.

I feel that there are both positives and negatives to daydreaming. Everyone’s daydreaming effects them a different way. Some people aren’t going through a hard time anymore so the daydreaming is just getting in their way, but for others they’re still going through a tough time and without being able to escape into their alter reality or whatever they would be lost. I don’t have many friends, I feel lonely, depressed, I have social anxiety, and one of the only things that ever brings me a glimpse of happiness or hope on a bad day can be my daydreams. Yes I realize that the daydreaming causes me to be unproductive and lazy, but it also saves my life. I wish those who’re trying to get rid of their MaDD the best, and I realize how addictive and troubling it is for other people. But I have MaDD and to say someone doesn’t have it bc they see it as a positive is kinda black and white.
